legibility: All 15 crops show every sign complete with its printed label legible. Best for tracing 1533: McGill (5560 px page) and LoC (3344-3575 px master JP2); Jung/e-rara (2550 px) is good but has two imperfect rings in the Malachim. 1651: the archive.org 'threebooksoccult' scan is cleaner than Wellcome, which has heavy show-through; Wellcome is the copy with a stated rights mark.
problems: 1651 Wellcome copy: strong show-through on all three pages (reversed ghosts of the facing table; on p. 441 the ruled grid of the p. 442 'nine chambers' figure). Tracers must ignore the faint strokes.
Jung copy (e-rara): Malachim Aleph top-middle ring prints open (Y-shaped) and the foot ring of the candlestick-shaped Samech prints as an open arc; LoC and McGill have closed rings.
archive.org 'threebooksoccult' (1651): community upload with no holding library or rights statement; treat as a cross-check, not as the named tracing source, until its provenance is confirmed.
McGill copy on archive.org: no rights statement in the item metadata.

1533 layout: Celestial in 3 rows of 9, 9 and 4 signs; Malachim 7, 7 and 9 (23 signs); Transitus fluvii 8, 7 and 7. 1651 layout: 7, 7, 8; Malachim 6, 5, 7, 5 (23 signs); 7, 8, 7. Every table runs right to left with the label set above each sign.

Two typesettings of 1533 pp. 273-274 were seen. Setting A (LoC, McGill, and the NLM copy archive.org 2213011R.nlm.nih.gov, leaves n290-n291, viewed but not cropped): recto misnumbered 'CCXLXXIII', Celestial row-1 labels with full stops, 'Shin' in Celestial and Malachim. Setting B (Jung/e-rara): 'CCLXXIII', no full stops, 'Schin' (Celestial) and 'Scin' (Malachim), and different line endings and spellings in the text (e.g. 'fragmēta' for 'fragmenta'). The signs look the same in both settings: in Malachim row 3 their positions, as fractions of the row width, agree within about 0.5% across LoC, McGill and Jung. That suggests the signs were printed from the same cuts while the labels were reset, but it is not proven.

McGill copy: the Theban table on p. 273 lacks the 'K' label (a dot stands in its place); LoC and NLM, in the same setting, print 'K'. This is a press variant, relevant to the Theban plates. Checked: NLM n290 prints 'K'. The Jung copy (setting B) prints a lower-case 'k'.

1533 to 1651 sign variant seen: in the Celestial, the 1651 Gimel has a third ring at the foot of its vertical (1533: rings only at the top of the vertical and the left end of the bar). The other Celestial signs and the Malachim and Transitus signs agree in structure on visual comparison (not measured stroke by stroke).
